Title: GSMC Student Appointed New Communications Staff at AKU Uganda
NewsSummary: Proscovia Nabatte aims to bridge her coursework with her new role on staff
NewsContent:
​

Proscovia Nabatte has always believed in the power of storytelling. Now, she's living one of her own, navigating a unique chapter as both a Master's student at Aga Khan University's Graduate School of Media and Communications (GSMC) and the newly appointed Communications and Marketing Specialist for AKU in Uganda.

“It's a mix of emotions," Proscovia says with a smile. “Being both a student and now a staff member at Aga Khan University feels surreal. It's a role that demands a lot; balancing academics with professional responsibilities, especially in such a pivotal communications role for the Uganda campus and Nakawa Specialty Centre."

Currently pursuing a Master of Arts in Strategic Communications, Proscovia describes her new position as more than a job. It's an opportunity to live out her coursework in real time.

“This experience is already expanding my career perspective, and it's exactly the kind of professional development I've always hoped for," she says. “Even in these first few days, I've realized that working at AKU demands deep knowledge and a constant growth mindset, nationally, regionally, and internationally."

Her passion for the programme at GSMC is clear. “Back in 2019, I was looking for a postgraduate programme that would fit the realities of being a communications professional. Most of what I found leaned too heavily on theory," she recalls. “This course is different. It's grounded in the real world. Practical case studies, strategic thinking, and storytelling I can immediately apply in my work."

That immediacy is part of what makes Proscovia's journey so striking. Her role requires her to lead communications and marketing initiatives for both AKU's academics and health services in Uganda – while balancing her own coursework.

“When I first visited the new campus at Nakawa, two words came to mind: impact and quality," she says. “It's not just the architecture; it's what the presence of AKU here means. For many years, Ugandans had to travel to Nairobi for specialized healthcare or postgraduate studies. Now, that level of excellence is right here at home."

And she's wasting no time putting theory into action. “One of the strongest tools I'm bringing into this role is storytelling," she says. “We've moved beyond direct marketing. Today, storytelling is the most effective form of engagement. I plan to integrate public relations, advocacy, strategic marketing, and communications into a single, purpose-driven model."

It's rare to find someone whose professional and academic lives align so closely. For AKU in Uganda, Proscovia Nabatte represents a promising bridge between vision and execution, theory and practice, and the future of communications in East Africa.
